stories.summary: Researchers have found a way to turn a cancer-fueling protein into a weapon against tumors. Activating this protein in immune cells helped them attack cancer and slow its growth in laboratory experiments.
stories.title: A protein that fuels cancer could also be the key to fighting it

stories.summary: Recent research suggests that a saline injection could offer long-lasting relief from carpal tunnel pain. The method provides an alternative treatment option without relying on steroids.
stories.title: A Saline Injection Could Offer Longer Relief From Carpal Tunnel Pain

stories.summary: A new study has found that spending time in nature is linked to healthier eating habits. Researchers suggest that exposure to natural environments can positively influence people's relationship with food.
stories.title: Contact With Nature is Linked to Healthy Eating, Shows Encouraging New Study

stories.summary: Researchers at Toronto Metropolitan University are studying the links between menopause, memory, and overall brain health. The work aims to address historical gaps in research regarding women's mental health.
stories.title: TMU research examines menopause, memory and brain health

stories.summary: An Oregon couple facing financial hardship received a brand new heating and cooling system valued at $16,000 for free. The installation was provided through a local community assistance program.
stories.title: Retired Couple Surprised With New HVAC System Worth $16k in a ‘Feel the Love’ Program That’s Aided 3100 Folks

stories.summary: Researchers report that hybrid quantum computers combining different technological approaches may soon become a reality. This advancement brings the field closer to more powerful and practical quantum systems.
stories.title: Best of Both Worlds: 'Hybrid' Quantum Computers Could Be Just Around The Corner, Researchers Say

stories.summary: Waterloo Region is expected to enjoy a week of clear, sunny weather following recent rain. The break from cloudy skies offers residents an opportunity to spend time outdoors before colder weather arrives.
stories.title: Sunshine takes over Waterloo Region’s forecast for upcoming week

stories.summary: Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 protected mice from the harmful effects of a high-salt diet. Supplemented mice showed lower blood pressure and improved memory compared to others.
stories.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt

stories.summary: Physicists have discovered a new quantum state of matter called a fractional Fermi sea using ultracold atoms. This finding challenges established theories and hints at the existence of exotic quasiparticles.
stories.title: Physicists create a bizarre new quantum state called a fractional fermi sea

stories.summary: A small study found that older adults who consumed blueberries daily experienced greater reductions in depressive symptoms. Researchers also observed changes in gut microbes, pointing to a potential gut-brain connection.
stories.title: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood

stories.summary: Researchers discovered that a psychedelic compound from magic mushrooms can calm highly aggressive fish without disrupting social interactions. The finding suggests potential future applications in managing aggression.
stories.title: Magic mushroom ingredient takes the fight out of aggressive fish

stories.summary: The Earth Sciences Museum at the University of Waterloo is hosting its annual Gem and Mineral Show. Attendees can explore a wide variety of rocks, gems, and educational exhibits across multiple buildings.
stories.title: Gem and mineral show set for return to the University of Waterloo

stories.summary: Researchers have identified specific brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief from deep brain stimulation. The findings could help improve future treatment placement for severe depression.
stories.title: Scientists uncover 3 key brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief

stories.summary: Scientists note that beneficial brown fat can be activated in the body using a specific blood pressure drug. This research highlights potential pathways for physical and metabolic health boosts.
stories.title: Brown Fat Can Be Beneficial For The Body – And a Blood Pressure Drug Could Turn It On

stories.summary: Three scientists recently won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their research in optogenetics. Medical columnist Dr. Peter Lin explained how this field of science works.
stories.title: What is optogenetics? Dr. Peter Lin explains

stories.summary: Scientists have found that male and female skin repair themselves using different cellular mechanisms. This discovery helps explain why wounds tend to heal faster in female tissue.
stories.title: Scientists discover that male and female skin play by different rules

stories.summary: A Guelph entrepreneur has created a functional chocolate bar designed to help relieve period pain naturally. The product offers women an alternative option for managing discomfort.
stories.title: Experiencing period pain? This Guelph entrepreneur created a chocolate that can help

stories.summary: Toronto is expected to experience pleasant, mainly sunny weather with a high of 16 C. Clear skies are forecasted for the area throughout the day.
stories.title: Toronto's Oct. 18 forecast: Mainly sunny

stories.summary: Two eateries in St. Catharines and Lincoln were awarded Bib Gourmand distinctions by the Michelin Guide. The recognition highlights local food establishments offering quality dining at affordable prices.
stories.title: St. Catharines bistro, Lincoln bakehouse receive Michelin distinction for quality, affordability

stories.summary: A new injection triggers the self-destruction of specific fat cells in clinical trials. The treatment shows promise for preventing weight regain after other interventions.
stories.title: A New Injection Makes Fat Cells Self-Destruct, And Might Prevent GLP-1 Weight Regain

stories.summary: A 99-year-old woman has officially become the world's oldest wing-walker after being strapped to the top of a small plane. The achievement came after encouragement from staff at her assisted-living facility.
stories.title: 99-yo Woman Snags ‘World’s Oldest Wing-Walker’ Title – 3 Months After Another Gran Did It (LOOK)

stories.summary: Radio host Craig Norris showcased a lineup of Ontario musical artists on a recent broadcast. The feature highlighted songs from performers including Majid Jordan, Peach Luffe, and Valley.
stories.title: In The Key Of C: Hear Majid Jordan, Peach Luffe, Mormor, Faiza, Valley and more

stories.summary: A severely overweight bulldog that struggled with mobility and health issues has successfully lost weight. The dog has now been placed in a new, loving home.
stories.title: Massive 70lb Dog the Size of Baby Hippo Sheds Pounds and Gets New Home

stories.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has mapped an orderly weather system on a planet twenty light-years away. This breakthrough gives scientists a new method for studying distant atmospheres.
stories.title: NASA’s Webb reveals the wild weather of a mysterious world 20 light-years away

stories.summary: Local sous chefs shared their favorite comfort food meals to eat when recovering from a cold or flu. Columnist Jasmine Mangalaseril compiled their recommended recipes and food tips.
stories.title: Need to feed a cold? Here's what local sous chefs eat when they're under the weather

stories.summary: Kitchener singer-songwriter Matthew Ryan Jacobs is returning to live performances and releasing a new album titled Cardinals. He reflected on his journey back to the stage in an interview with CBC K-W.
stories.title: Kitchener's Matthew Ryan Jacobs set to release new album

stories.summary: A long-term study discovered that certain forest soils are absorbing more methane from the atmosphere as temperatures rise. This unexpected natural process shows increasing resilience in forest ecosystems.
stories.title: A 24-year study uncovers a surprising climate benefit beneath forests

stories.summary: A new documentary celebrating Toronto's famous 1972 production of the musical Godspell is screening at Hamilton's Playhouse Cinema. Original cast member Jayne Eastwood will participate in a live Q&A session following the film.
stories.title: New documentary about legendary 1972 Godspell cast screens at Playhouse, Q&A with star Jayne Eastwood

stories.summary: A women's group in an Indonesian village is successfully restoring local mangroves while creating new economic opportunities. The initiative helps protect coastal ecosystems and empowers female community members.
stories.title: Indonesian women cash in on mangrove restoration: Interview with community leader Wisye Sahambangung

stories.summary: Researchers have detailed the relationship between deep sleep and growth hormone regulation. The findings could lead to new treatments for sleep and neurological disorders.
stories.title: Scientists discover how deep sleep builds muscle, burns fat, and boosts the brain

stories.summary: A recent SpaceX cargo delivery to the International Space Station includes miniature brain models and 3D heart tissue. Scientists plan to use these samples to research new treatments for brain diseases and failing eyesight.
stories.title: SpaceX just delivered some very strange cargo to the International Space Station

stories.summary: Anthropic has joined a $10-billion data centre project in Nova Scotia. The facility aims to support advanced technology development in the region.
stories.title: Anthropic signs onto $10-billion Nova Scotia data centre project

stories.summary: A former SickKids president delivered an encouraging commencement address to recent Brock University graduates. The speech urged students to embrace optimism when facing future challenges.
stories.title: ‘Choose optimism,’ former SickKids President urges Brock grads

stories.summary: Two Brock University students were awarded the Spirit of Brock medal for their advocacy work. The recipients are dedicated to ensuring student voices are heard and represented.
stories.title: Gallery: Community changemakers celebrated with Spirit of Brock medal

stories.summary: The province of Manitoba has officially declared that its measles outbreak is now over. The outbreak had been active for more than a year and a half.
stories.title: Measles outbreak declared over in Manitoba

stories.summary: Nyaradzo Auxilia Hoto became one of Zimbabwe's pioneering wildlife rangers, overcoming past struggles to build a stable career. Her journey highlights inspiring new opportunities for women in conservation.
stories.title: The uplifting story of one of Zimbabwe’s pioneering women rangers

stories.summary: Brock University psychology researcher Hamnah Shahid is focusing her work on reducing social stigma surrounding mental health and addiction. Her research aims to drive progressive policy and community support.
stories.title: Psychology grad strives to combat stigma around mental health and addiction

stories.summary: Analysis of the Orion spacecraft's heat shield following the Artemis II mission confirmed its thermal protection system worked successfully. The rigorous evaluation verified that the shield adequately protected the crew during atmospheric reentry.
stories.title: Artemis II Heat Shield After Splashdown

stories.summary: Field tests of a new textile called Plant Armor showed it can triple strawberry yields while reducing water and pesticide use. The protective fabric simply drapes over patches to improve crop health.
stories.title: Drape Some ‘Plant Armor’ Fabric Over a Strawberry Patch to Triple Yields with Less Pesticides

stories.summary: Recent positive global developments include a plummeting poverty rate in Indonesia and a new era of environmental recovery for the River Thames. Additionally, North America has opened a massive wildlife bridge to protect animals.
stories.title: What went right this week: the good news that matters

stories.summary: Researchers discovered that atomic steps can guide quantum vortices through superconductors in a single direction. This control could lead to the development of ultra-efficient superconducting electronics.
stories.title: A quantum highway just one atom high could transform superconductors

stories.summary: Researchers have discovered how exercise can help reverse damage caused by muscle aging. Physical activity restores balance to a gene that interferes with muscle repair and protein clearing.
stories.title: Scientists discover how exercise reverses muscle aging
